doc_kind: Medicaid medical policy (Healthy Blue Louisiana; SURG.00121 draft with redline marks; library labels it Carelon)
lines_of_business: Healthy Blue Louisiana Medicaid ('Healthy Blue's standard Medicaid benefit plan')
effective_or_revised: SURG.00121; draft shows 'Publish Date 12/29/202108/18/2022' and 'Last Review Date 08/112/20221' (overstruck dates; latest revision history 08/11/2022)
sections_in_order: Position Statement (Medically Necessary; Not Medically Necessary; Investigational)
criteria_location: Position Statement, pp.1-4 (of 42): TAVR (native), valve-in-valve, transcatheter mitral edge-to-edge repair, transcatheter pulmonary valve, then not-medically-necessary and investigational lists. The remaining ~38 pages are rationale, trial tables, device tables, codes and references.
procedures_covered: Cerebral embolic protection (33370) appears only in the code list, as potentially medically necessary; no criterion addresses it

logic.top_level: pathways (TAVR native has 2 age-based risk pathways; valve-in-valve; mitral; pulmonary)

k_of_n.quote: The individual has severe degenerative, native valve aortic stenosis demonstrated by one of the following
The individual is in one of the following categories: 1. Age 65 years or older ... or 2. Age younger than 65 with intermediate or greater open surgical risk

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: No contraindication list; 'Not Medically Necessary' statement when criteria not met; investigational for tricuspid and for mitral annuloplasty and mitral ViV.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Valve-in-valve for failed prior open surgical bioprosthesis is the only follow-on case.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: 1. Age 65 years or older with Lowany open surgical risk and 65 years of age or older; or
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Redline text: 'Low' struck and 'any' inserted plus a duplicated '65 years of age or older'; History says 08/12/2021 'Revised MN criteria for TAVR in low open surgical risk to include individuals 65 years of age or older', so the intent is 'any open surgical risk and age >= 65'.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: 2. Age younger than 65 with Iintermediate or greater open surgical risk (predicted risk of surgical mortality at 30 days greater than or equal to 3%) as determined by at least two physicians.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'as determined by at least two physicians' could apply only to this branch or to all of C; capital 'I' is a redline fragment.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: either a mean aortic valve gradient of more than 40 mm Hg; or 4. a peak aortic-jet velocity of more than 4.0 m/sec; and
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'either' appears on item 3 only but the list is 4 items; item 3 and 4 are strict >, items 1,2 are <=.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: at high or greater risk for open surgical therapy (that is, Society of Thoracic Surgeons operative risk score greater than or equal to 8% or at a 15% or greater risk of operative mortality at 30 days)
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'or' between STS score and mortality estimate; who chooses is 'at least two physicians'.

Heart failure symptoms of New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II or greater
severe degenerative, native valve aortic stenosis
Age 65 years or older with any open surgical risk; Age younger than 65 with intermediate or greater open surgical risk (>= 3% 30-day mortality) as determined by at least two physicians
failure of previous open surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve; high or greater risk (STS >= 8% or >= 15% 30-day mortality) as determined by at least two physicians
TAVR using a U.S Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved device*
Echocardiogram demonstrates that the primary regurgitant jet results from malcoaptation of the A2 and P2 scallops
Existence of a full (circumferential) right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) conduit that was equal to or greater than 16 mm in diameter when originally implanted

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: Codes grouped under 'When services may be Medically Necessary when criteria are met' and a not-covered group; ICD-10 procedure 02RF3JH/02RF3JZ/02RF4JZ listed; ICD-10 diagnosis 'All diagnoses'.
codes.non_covered_code_lists: Separate groups 'When services are Not Medically Necessary' and 'Investigational and Not Medically Necessary' (33418, 33419, 33999 when specified as transcatheter replacement, 0345T, 0483T, 0484T, 0544T, 0545T, 0569T, 0570T, 0646T). Note 33370 (cerebral embolic protection) sits in the 'may be Medically Necessary when criteria are met' list although the position statement never mentions cerebral protection.

extraction_hazards: Redline artifacts in the criteria text: 'Lowany', 'Iintermediate', '12/29/202108/18/20 22', '08/112/20221'
Boilerplate legal paragraph (about 12 lines) repeats on every one of 42 pages and splits the position statement mid-list (criterion C ends page 1, items 1-2 start page 2)
Trial comparison table with merged columns (pp.5-6) contains percentages that are not criteria
Device approval table lists indications with risk thresholds (e.g., 'predicted risk of surgical mortality >= 3%') that differ from the policy criteria
Five policy families in one document (aortic, ViV, mitral, pulmonary, tricuspid)
interesting_structures: Age-gated risk rule: age >= 65 any risk; age < 65 needs intermediate or greater risk (age-banded pathways)
Policy revised in 2021 to move from 'high risk' to 'any risk' for age >= 65, reflecting FDA label expansion
Device approval table in Background acts as an implicit appendix of eligible devices
Cerebral embolic protection code 33370 is listed as potentially covered, the opposite of Florida Blue and UHC (investigational/unproven)

fit_to_tree.why: Nested any/all with numeric leaves fits well, but redline corruption in the key age/risk clause and 'determined by at least two physicians' need human reading.
